title: Lighthouse metrics→trace runway — design notes + rollout checklist
content:
Context and intent:

This doc captures a compact, high‑signal observability plan we can use as a "lighthouse" during model and infra rollouts. The goal is not to collect every metric; it is to define a minimal, well‑instrumented runway of metrics + trace anchors that let operators and product engineers quickly detect regressions in latency, cost, and correctness for tokenized inference.

Why "lighthouse"?
- Small, stable signal set for rollout gating.
- Cheap to query (designed for microdash panels + synthetic probes).
- Good correlation surface for fast drill‑downs (metrics -> traces -> prompt replay).

Design principles (short):
1) Metric names are contractable and immutable for rollout windows.
2) Keep cardinality low on the critical path (tenant, model_version, route).
3) Provide 1–2 high‑priority trace anchors per metric to accelerate RCA.
4) Alerting uses multi‑window judgement (5m spike + 1h drift) to reduce noise.
5) Query cost budget: lighthouse panels should run on 1h rollups by default and 5m for live probes.

Lighthouse metric definitions (canonical table):
- inference.latency.p50: description: median time from request received to first token emitted; unit: ms; collection: per request; labels: model_version, region, route, tenant; owner: eng-serving-runtime; SLO target: p50 < 90ms for hosted tier; alert: sustained p50 > 150ms for 10m.
- inference.latency.p95: description: p95 end-to-end latency for tokenized responses; unit: ms; labels same as p50; owner: eng-serving-runtime; SLO target: p95 < 400ms; alert: p95 > 800ms for 10m OR p95 increase > 40% vs baseline for 1h.
- inference.kvcache.warmth: description: fraction of requests that hit a warmed KV cache prefix; unit: ratio (0..1); labels: model_version, tenant; owner: serving-runtime/caching; collection: sampled per request (100% for internal); alert: drop > 15% absolute vs baseline for 30m.
- inference.tokens.per_request.avg: description: average generated tokens per request (excludes prompt tokens); unit: count; labels: route, model_version; owner: product/hosted-api; use: cost normalization on dashboards.
- inference.cpu.gpu.utilization.pool: description: pool-level GPU utilization average over window; unit: pct; labels: capacity_pool, region; owner: infra-capacity; alert: sustained > 85% for 15m without autoscaler activity.
- inference.error.rate: description: fraction of requests returning 5xx or internal error; unit: ratio; labels: error_bucket, model_version, route; owner: eng-sre; alert: > 0.5% for 5m or doubling from baseline for 1h.
- inference.reroute.fallback.count: description: count of requests routed to fallback models due to capacity/latency policy; unit: count; labels: from_model, to_model, route; owner: routing; use: monitor graceful degradation.

Metric conventions and derivations (notes):
- All latency metrics should be measured server‑side at the routing edge and include queuing time. Distinguish client‑perceived ttf (time‑to‑first‑token) vs server internal generation time in detailed panels.
- Warmth: compute as (requests_with_kv_hit / total_sampled_requests) with sampling deterministic per tenant to keep cardinality low.
- Token economics panels must normalize by tokens.per_request.avg and price_per_token (from billing export).

Tracing strategy (anchors and sampling):
Primary goal: traces should provide a fast pivot from a failing lighthouse metric to the exact token path and model shards involved.
- Span model: request -> router -> model-server -> kv-cache -> kernel-exec; each span must include stable tags: request_id, prompt_digest (sha1), model_version, route, tenant_id (hashed for PII), seq_len, kv_hit (bool), shard_id.
- Sampling policy: adaptive two-tier sampling.
  - Tier A (high fidelity): sample 100% of traces for synthetic probes and canary routes; 10% of real user traffic for tenants in rollout cohorts.
  - Tier B (sparse): sample 0.5% of requests across other traffic, with higher sampling if p95 latency crosses threshold.
- Trace payload caps: limit returned token-by-token payloads in traces to first 256 tokens to avoid storage blowup; full prompt is stored as a prompt_digest and an internal prompt-replay store (access controlled).
- Sensitive data handling: redact free-form user text in traces for teams without DPA/contract; store hashed tenant_id and hashed prompt_digest only (link to private prompt store requires security ticket).
- Enrichment: traces should attach a small evaluation fingerprint when available (eval_id) and model quantization_profile tag (FP16/INT8).

Dashboard layout suggestions (microdash first):
- Panel group: "Lighthouse — Latency & Cache"
  - p50/p95 sparkline (5m/1h) with anomaly overlay
  - kv warmth heatmap (tenant vs time) small multiples for top 10 tenants
  - p95 correlation scatter: p95 vs kv_warmth (model_version color) (query cost: use 1h rollup window)
- Panel group: "Capacity & Fallbacks"
  - GPU pool utilization + autoscaler events timeline
  - reroute.fallback.count stacked by reason and to_model (last 24h)
- Panel group: "Errors & Regression Signals"
  - error.rate by error_bucket (5m) + trace link button for top error fingerprint
  - prompt_digest anomaly list: top 20 prompt digests causing >10% of p95 outliers (manual triage list)
- Drilldown flow: clicking a high p95 point -> opens timeboxed traces (5m window) filtered by model_version/route and prepopulated prompt replay (if permitted).

Query cost and rollup guidance:
- Default lighthouse dashboards use 1h aggregations for historic panels and 5m for live operator panels.
- Avoid per‑token grouping in lighthouse (use for deep investigation only).
- Add a query cost footer on each dashboard (approx cost estimate for last 24h queries) — useful for SRE when running heavy investigations.

Rollout checklist (pre‑rollout -> rollout -> post‑rollout):
Pre‑rollout (owner: eng-release + observability):
- Freeze metric names & tags for rollout window (no renames).
- Synthetic probe harness: define 3 probes (short prompt, long prompt, multi-hop) that exercise kv cache and full model path. Verify traces for those probes are sampling at Tier A.
- Baseline capture: capture 72h baseline of p50/p95, kv_warmth, tokens.per_request.avg, error.rate; store snapshot and attach as rollout artifact.
- Dashboard smoke: light dashboard with toggle to compare current to baseline (owner: obs).

Rollout (owner: release manager):
- Enable canary (1% tenants) + ramp schedule; validate synthetic probes green after each step.
- Monitor lighthouse p95 + kv_warmth and error.rate for canary cohort for first 30m after step.
- If p95 increases > 30% vs baseline OR kv_warmth drops > 10% absolute -> halt and capture traces.

Post‑rollout / regression hunting (owner: eng-sre + model team):
- If any alert fires, run pivot: metric -> trace anchor -> prompt digest top list -> prompt replay. Use trace tags to find shard hotspots.
- Capture RCA doc with exact metric snapshots and 3 example traces attached.

Open questions and TODOs:
- How to surface cross‑tenant cold‑cache effects without exploding cardinality? Proposal: synthetic tenant cohort + tenant_weighted_warmth metric.
- Should we add a lightweight trace summary store for top n prompt_digests? (tradeoffs: storage vs speed of triage).
- Privacy gating: finalize redaction policy for EU tenants under DPA.

Appendix: quick alert rules (suggested):
- alert: LighthouseHighP95Spike
  - expr: increase(inference.latency.p95[10m]) > 0.25 and inference.latency.p95 > 500
  - for: 10m
  - severity: page

- alert: KVWarmthDrop
  - expr: (baseline_kv_warmth - inference.kvcache.warmth) > 0.15
  - for: 30m
  - severity: ticket

- alert: InferenceErrorSurge
  - expr: rate(inference.error.count[5m]) / rate(inference.request.count[5m]) > 0.005
  - for: 5m

Slack workflows / playbooks to attach to alerts: quick triage template with trace links, sample prompts, and rollback instructions (owner: eng-oncall).

Contacts and owners: Ava Patel (observability lead), Marcus Chen (serving runtime), Lena Ortiz (dashboard/UX), Daniel Park (tracing infra), Priya Singh (privacy/compliance).

Notes to self: keep this doc intentionally compact. If we need a full instrument spec, split into "lighthouse-instrument-spec" annex.
